records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע יִתְר֨וֹ כֹהֵ֤ן מִדְיָן֙ חֹתֵ֣ן מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֵת֩ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ לְמֹשֶׁ֔ה וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַמּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־הוֹצִ֧יא יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And heard Jethro, [the] priest of Midian, [the] father-in-law of Moses, all that had done God for Moses and for Israel his people, that had brought out Yahweh Israel from Egypt.
pieces: Word reached Jethro, the priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, of everything God had done for Moses and for Israel, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had brought Israel out of Egypt.

L.1: And Jethro, the priest of Midian, the father-in-law of Moses, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had brought Israel out from Egypt.

R.1: Jethro was the priest of Midian and the father-in-law of Moses. He heard about all the things God had done for Moses and for Israel, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. He heard how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had brought Israel out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: Jethro, priest of Midian, Moses' father-in-law
decisions.reason: Jethro is the priest of Midian whose daughter Zipporah married Moses (2:16-21; 3:1). He is called Reuel in 2:18 and Jether in 4:18. Moses had left him to return to Egypt (4:18).

decisions.choice: that Yahweh had brought Israel out: the sum of what Jethro heard
decisions.reason: The second clause sums up "all that God had done": the great deed was bringing Israel out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: Word reached Jethro
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "Jethro heard" around so that the long description of Jethro does not separate the subject from the verb.

records.heading: Jethro's visit and advice

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֗ח יִתְרוֹ֙ חֹתֵ֣ן מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶת־צִפֹּרָ֖ה אֵ֣שֶׁת מֹשֶׁ֑ה אַחַ֖ר שִׁלּוּחֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And had taken Jethro, [the] father-in-law of Moses, Zipporah, [the] wife of Moses, after her sendings away,
pieces: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, had taken in Zipporah, Moses' wife, after Moses had sent her back,

L.2: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, took Zipporah, the wife of Moses, after her sending away,

R.2: Moses had sent his wife Zipporah back to her family, and her father Jethro had taken her in.

decisions.choice: after her sending away: after Moses had sent her back to her father
decisions.reason: The text does not say when or why Moses sent Zipporah and the boys back. The last time they appear, they are traveling with him toward Egypt (4:20, 24-26). The same verb is used of sending a wife away in divorce (Deuteronomy 24:1), and the noun is used of a parting gift (1 Kings 9:16). Here the story treats Zipporah as still Moses' wife (verses 2, 6), so a return to her father's house for safety is the more likely sense.

decisions.choice: Moses had sent her back
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only a noun, "her sending away". Balanced and Readable name Moses as the one who sent her and say where she went.

records.source: וְאֵ֖ת שְׁנֵ֣י בָנֶ֑יהָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר שֵׁ֤ם הָֽאֶחָד֙ גֵּֽרְשֹׁ֔ם כִּ֣י אָמַ֔ר גֵּ֣ר הָיִ֔יתִי בְּאֶ֖רֶץ נָכְרִיָּֽה׃
records.gloss: and her two sons, of whom [the] name of the one [was] Gershom, for he had said, a sojourner I have been in a land foreign,
pieces: along with her two sons. One of them was named Gershom, because Moses had said, "I have been an outsider in a foreign land."

L.3: and her two sons, of whom the name of the one [was] Gershom, for he said, "A sojourner I have been in a foreign land,"

R.3: He had also taken in her two sons. One son was named Gershom, which sounds like the Hebrew words for "a stranger there." Moses had named him that because he said, "I have been a stranger in a foreign land."

decisions.choice: Gershom ... a sojourner: a play on the name
decisions.reason: The name Gershom sounds like the words for "a sojourner there". The saying repeats 2:22 word for word. A sojourner is someone who lives in a land that is not his own.

decisions.choice: her two sons: Gershom and Eliezer
decisions.reason: Only Gershom's birth is told (2:22), though 4:20 speaks of Moses' "sons". Eliezer is named here for the first time (verse 4).

decisions.choice: which sounds like the Hebrew words for "a stranger there"
decisions.reason: As at 2:22, Readable explains the play on the name, which is lost without it.

records.source: וְשֵׁ֥ם הָאֶחָ֖ד אֱלִיעֶ֑זֶר כִּֽי־אֱלֹהֵ֤י אָבִי֙ בְּעֶזְרִ֔י וַיַּצִּלֵ֖נִי מֵחֶ֥רֶב פַּרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: and [the] name of the one [was] Eliezer, for [the] God of my father [was] in my help, and he delivered me from [the] sword of Pharaoh.
pieces: The other was named Eliezer, because "The God of my father was my helper, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescued me from Pharaoh's sword."

L.4: and the name of the other [was] Eliezer, for "The God of my father [was] my help, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh."

R.4: The other son was named Eliezer, which means "My God is help." Moses had said, "The God of my father helped me. He saved me when Pharaoh wanted to kill me with the sword."

decisions.choice: Eliezer: "my God is help"
decisions.reason: The name Eliezer means "my God is help". The explanation takes up the same word: "the God of my father was my help".

decisions.choice: delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh
decisions.reason: Pharaoh tried to kill Moses after he struck down the Egyptian, and Moses fled to Midian (2:15). God's help then is a first taste of the deliverance Israel has now known (verses 8-10).

decisions.choice: the God of my father: the God of Moses' family
decisions.reason: Moses speaks of the God his ancestors worshiped, as God named himself at the bush (3:6).

decisions.choice: which means "My God is help." Moses had said
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the name and names the speaker, so the reader can see why the boy was named this way.

decisions.choice: when Pharaoh wanted to kill me with the sword
decisions.reason: Readable spells out "Pharaoh's sword" as Pharaoh's plan to kill Moses (2:15).

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֞א יִתְר֨וֹ חֹתֵ֥ן מֹשֶׁ֛ה וּבָנָ֥יו וְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה אֶל־הַמִּדְבָּ֗ר אֲשֶׁר־ה֛וּא חֹנֶ֥ה שָׁ֖ם הַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And came Jethro, [the] father-in-law of Moses, and his sons and his wife, to Moses into the wilderness where he [was] encamping there, [at the] mountain of God.
pieces: Moses' father-in-law Jethro came out into the wilderness with Moses' wife and sons, and found him camped at the mountain of God.

L.5: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, came, and his sons and his wife, to Moses into the wilderness where he was camping there, [at] the mountain of God.

R.5: Jethro came with Moses' wife and sons to meet Moses in the desert. Moses was camped near the mountain of God.

decisions.choice: the mountain of God: Horeb, also called Sinai
decisions.reason: This is the mountain where God met Moses at the bush (3:1, 12). Israel arrives there formally in 19:1-2, so this story may be told here ahead of time, grouped with the other stories of the journey.

decisions.choice: his sons and his wife: Moses' sons and wife
decisions.reason: "His" refers to Moses, who is named next, not to Jethro.

decisions.choice: Moses' wife and sons
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Moses to make clear whose family it is. Literal keeps "his sons and his wife".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֲנִ֛י חֹתֶנְךָ֥ יִתְר֖וֹ בָּ֣א אֵלֶ֑יךָ וְאִ֨שְׁתְּךָ֔ וּשְׁנֵ֥י בָנֶ֖יהָ עִמָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And he said to Moses, I your father-in-law Jethro [am] coming to you, and your wife and her two sons with her.
pieces: He sent word to Moses, "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am on my way to you, along with your wife and her two sons."

L.6: And he said to Moses, "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you, and your wife and her two sons with her."

R.6: He sent a message ahead to Moses: "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to see you. Your wife and her two sons are with me."

decisions.choice: he said to Moses: a message sent ahead
decisions.reason: In the next verse Moses goes out to meet Jethro, so these words were most likely sent ahead by a messenger before Jethro arrived.

decisions.choice: I, your father-in-law: or "Look, your father-in-law"
alternatives: Look, your father-in-law Jethro is coming to you
decisions.reason: The Masoretic text has "I". The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Greek Septuagint are reported to read "look" (a word that differs by one letter) and to tell it as news brought to Moses: "Look, your father-in-law Jethro is coming to you." The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: sent word / sent a message ahead
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how the words reached Moses, since he goes out to meet Jethro afterward (verse 7).

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֨א מֹשֶׁ֜ה לִקְרַ֣את חֹֽתְנ֗וֹ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֨חוּ֙ וַיִּשַּׁק־ל֔וֹ וַיִּשְׁאֲל֥וּ אִישׁ־לְרֵעֵ֖הוּ לְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ הָאֹֽהֱלָה׃
records.gloss: And went out Moses to meet his father-in-law, and he bowed down and he kissed him, and they asked each his neighbor of welfare, and they went into the tent.
pieces: Moses went out to meet his father-in-law. He bowed low and kissed him, and they asked after each other's well-being. Then they went into the tent.

L.7: And Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, and he bowed down and kissed him, and they asked each his fellow about [his] welfare, and they went into the tent.

R.7: Moses went out to meet his father-in-law. He bowed down to show respect and kissed him. They asked each other how things had been going. Then they went into Moses' tent.

decisions.choice: he bowed down and kissed him: a greeting of honor and affection
decisions.reason: Bowing showed respect for an elder and a host; the kiss was a family greeting (Genesis 29:13; 33:4). Moses honors the man who once took him in (2:20-21).

decisions.choice: asked about welfare: asked how the other was
decisions.reason: The word is the familiar word for peace, meaning wholeness and well-being. To ask about someone's peace is to ask how they are (Genesis 43:27; 1 Samuel 17:22).

decisions.choice: Moses' tent
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the tent"; the setting shows it is Moses' own tent. Readable says so, and adds that the bow showed respect.

records.source: וַיְסַפֵּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ לְחֹ֣תְנ֔וֹ אֵת֩ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְפַרְעֹ֣ה וּלְמִצְרַ֔יִם עַ֖ל אוֹדֹ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֵ֤ת כָּל־הַתְּלָאָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מְצָאָ֣תַם בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וַיַּצִּלֵ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And recounted Moses to his father-in-law all that had done Yahweh to Pharaoh and to Egypt on account of Israel, all the hardship that had found them on the way, and delivered them Yahweh.
pieces: Moses gave his father-in-law a full account of what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done to Pharaoh and to Egypt on Israel's behalf. He told of every hardship that had come upon them on their journey, and of how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had delivered them.

L.8: And Moses recounted to his father-in-law all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done to Pharaoh and to Egypt on account of Israel, all the hardship that had found them on the way, and [how] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} delivered them.

R.8: Moses told his father-in-law everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians to help Israel. He told him about all the troubles they had faced on the way, and how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had rescued them.

decisions.choice: hardship: weariness, trouble
decisions.reason: The word means toil and the trouble that wears people down. It is used of Israel's trials in the wilderness in Numbers 20:14, and of its suffering in Nehemiah 9:32. Here it covers the troubles of chapters 14-17: the sea, the thirst, the hunger and Amalek.

decisions.choice: that had found them: that had come upon them
decisions.reason: Trouble is pictured as meeting or overtaking the traveler on the road.

records.source: וַיִּ֣חַדְּ יִתְר֔וֹ עַ֚ל כָּל־הַטּוֹבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִצִּיל֖וֹ מִיַּ֥ד מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And rejoiced Jethro over all the good that had done Yahweh to Israel, whom he had delivered from [the] hand of Egypt.
pieces: Jethro was glad because of all the good {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done for Israel when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescued them from the power of Egypt.

L.9: And Jethro rejoiced over all the good that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done to Israel, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had delivered from the hand of Egypt.

R.9: Jethro was very happy to hear about all the good things {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done for Israel. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had rescued them from the Egyptians.

decisions.choice: the hand of Egypt: Egypt's power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power and control (3:8; 14:30).

decisions.choice: rejoiced: was glad
decisions.reason: The verb is rare; it means to be glad or delighted. Jethro shares Israel's joy though he is not an Israelite.

decisions.choice: the power of Egypt / the Egyptians
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture of the "hand" means; Literal keeps it.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ יִתְרוֹ֒ בָּר֣וּךְ יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִצִּ֥יל אֶתְכֶ֛ם מִיַּ֥ד מִצְרַ֖יִם וּמִיַּ֣ד פַּרְעֹ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִצִּיל֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם מִתַּ֖חַת יַד־מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And said Jethro, blessed [be] Yahweh, who has delivered you from [the] hand of Egypt and from [the] hand of Pharaoh, who has delivered the people from under [the] hand of Egypt.
pieces: Jethro said, "Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has delivered you from the grip of Egypt and of Pharaoh, and has freed this people from under Egypt's hand.

L.10: And Jethro said, "Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of Pharaoh, who has delivered the people from under the hand of Egypt.

R.10: Jethro said, "Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! He has saved you from the Egyptians and from Pharaoh. He has set the people free from Egypt's control.

decisions.choice: blessed be Yahweh: praise to the LORD
decisions.reason: To bless God is to praise him and speak well of him for what he has done (Genesis 14:20; 24:27). Jethro, a priest of another people, blesses Israel's God by name.

decisions.choice: you ... the people: Moses and those with him, then Israel as a whole
decisions.reason: "You" is plural, meaning Moses and Aaron and the Israelites with them. The second clause restates the first for the whole people. Both clauses use the same verb, "delivered".

decisions.choice: Praise the LORD!
decisions.reason: Readable says "praise", the plain sense of blessing God. Literal and Balanced keep "blessed be".

records.source: עַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּֽי־גָד֥וֹל יְהוָ֖ה מִכָּל־הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֣י בַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר זָד֖וּ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Now I know that great [is] Yahweh more than all the gods, for in the matter in which they acted presumptuously against them.
pieces: Now I know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is greater than all the gods, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed it in the very matter in which they acted proudly against Israel."

L.11: Now I know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] greater than all the gods, for in the matter in which they acted presumptuously against them [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was above them]."

R.11: Now I know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is greater than all the gods. The Egyptians treated Israel with pride and scorn, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} showed that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was greater."

decisions.choice: in the matter in which they acted presumptuously against them: the sentence is incomplete and uncertain
alternatives: for he was above the gods in the very thing in which they acted proudly
he did this to those who acted proudly against Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew clause breaks off without saying what happened "in the matter". The most likely sense is that the LORD proved greater in the very thing in which the Egyptians acted proudly against Israel. Nehemiah 9:10 uses the same verb of the Egyptians: God knew that "they acted presumptuously against them". Another reading takes "they" to be the gods of Egypt, whom the LORD judged (12:12; Numbers 33:4).

decisions.choice: now I know that Yahweh is greater than all the gods
decisions.reason: Jethro comes to the knowledge the plagues were meant to bring: that the LORD has no equal (9:14; 15:11). The book says again and again that the nations "will know" the LORD (7:5; 14:4).

decisions.choice: [he was above them]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words the clause needs to be a sentence and brackets them.

decisions.choice: Israel / the Egyptians
decisions.reason: Balanced names Israel as "them"; Readable also names the Egyptians as "they". This follows the first reading in the meaning decision; the other reading is in the footnote.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֞ח יִתְר֨וֹ חֹתֵ֥ן מֹשֶׁ֛ה עֹלָ֥ה וּזְבָחִ֖ים לֵֽאלֹהִ֑ים וַיָּבֹ֨א אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְכֹ֣ל׀זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לֶאֱכָל־לֶ֛חֶם עִם־חֹתֵ֥ן מֹשֶׁ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And took Jethro, [the] father-in-law of Moses, a burnt offering and sacrifices for God, and came Aaron and all [the] elders of Israel to eat bread with [the] father-in-law of Moses before God.
pieces: Then Moses' father-in-law Jethro took a burnt offering and sacrifices and offered them to God. Aaron and every elder of Israel joined Moses' father-in-law, and they ate a meal together before God.

L.12: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God; and Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with the father-in-law of Moses before God.

R.12: Then Jethro brought a burnt offering and other sacrifices to God. Aaron and all the leaders of Israel came and ate a meal with Moses' father-in-law there in God's presence.

decisions.choice: a burnt offering and sacrifices
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was burned whole on the altar for God. The other sacrifices were animals whose meat was shared in a meal, part given to God and part eaten by the worshipers (Leviticus 3; 7:15).

decisions.choice: to eat bread: to share a meal
decisions.reason: "Bread" stands for food in general. Eating together before God sealed fellowship between Jethro and the leaders of Israel (compare 24:11).

decisions.choice: before God: in God's presence
decisions.reason: The meal was eaten in God's presence, probably at the altar where the sacrifices were offered, near the mountain of God (verse 5).

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for "elders", as elsewhere in Exodus.

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב מֹשֶׁ֖ה לִשְׁפֹּ֣ט אֶת־הָעָ֑ם וַיַּעֲמֹ֤ד הָעָם֙ עַל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה מִן־הַבֹּ֖קֶר עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: And it was on the next day, and sat Moses to judge the people, and stood the people by Moses from the morning until the evening.
pieces: The following day Moses sat down to judge the people's cases, and from morning to evening the people stood waiting before him.

L.13: And it was on the next day, and Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood by Moses from the morning until the evening.

R.13: The next day Moses sat down to settle the people's arguments. People stood around him waiting from morning until evening.

decisions.choice: to judge: to decide disputes and give rulings
decisions.reason: To judge here is to hear cases and settle disputes between people (verse 16), not only to pass sentence on wrongdoers.

decisions.choice: sat: took the judge's seat
decisions.reason: A judge sat to hear cases while those who brought them stood (Judges 4:5; Ruth 4:1-2).

decisions.choice: waiting
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say why the people stood: they were waiting their turn.

records.source: וַיַּרְא֙ חֹתֵ֣ן מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־ה֥וּא עֹשֶׂ֖ה לָעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מָֽה־הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתָּ֤ה עֹשֶׂה֙ לָעָ֔ם מַדּ֗וּעַ אַתָּ֤ה יוֹשֵׁב֙ לְבַדֶּ֔ךָ וְכָל־הָעָ֛ם נִצָּ֥ב עָלֶ֖יךָ מִן־בֹּ֥קֶר עַד־עָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: And saw [the] father-in-law of Moses all that he [was] doing for the people, and he said, what [is] the thing this that you [are] doing for the people? Why [are] you sitting by yourself, and all the people standing by you from morning until evening?
pieces: When Moses' father-in-law saw all that he was doing for the people, he said, "What sort of thing is this you are doing with the people? Why do you sit here alone, while the whole crowd stands waiting on you from morning to evening?"

L.14: And the father-in-law of Moses saw all that he was doing for the people, and he said, "What [is] this thing that you are doing for the people? Why are you sitting by yourself, and all the people standing by you from morning until evening?"

R.14: Moses' father-in-law saw all the work Moses was doing for the people. He asked, "Why are you doing all this by yourself? All these people are standing around you from morning until evening!"

decisions.choice: what ... why: questions of surprise and concern
decisions.reason: Jethro is not asking for information; his questions show that he thinks something is wrong with the way Moses is working (verse 17).

decisions.choice: by yourself: alone
decisions.reason: The word "alone" is the point of the complaint. It returns in verse 18: "you are not able to do it alone".

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה לְחֹתְנ֑וֹ כִּֽי־יָבֹ֥א אֵלַ֛י הָעָ֖ם לִדְרֹ֥שׁ אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to his father-in-law, because comes to me the people to inquire of God.
pieces: Moses answered his father-in-law, "It is because the people come to me to inquire of God.

L.15: And Moses said to his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me to inquire of God.

R.15: Moses answered, "The people come to me to find out what God wants them to do.

decisions.choice: to inquire of God: to seek God's answer or ruling
decisions.reason: To inquire of God is to ask for his word on a matter, often through a prophet or priest (Genesis 25:22; 1 Samuel 9:9; 1 Kings 22:8). Here it means bringing cases to Moses for a ruling that comes from God (verse 16).

decisions.choice: to find out what God wants them to do
decisions.reason: Readable explains "inquire of God" in plain words.

records.source: כִּֽי־יִהְיֶ֨ה לָהֶ֤ם דָּבָר֙ בָּ֣א אֵלַ֔י וְשָׁ֣פַטְתִּ֔י בֵּ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ וּבֵ֣ין רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְהוֹדַעְתִּ֛י אֶת־חֻקֵּ֥י הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים וְאֶת־תּוֹרֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: When it is to them a matter, coming to me, and I judge between a man and between his neighbor, and I make known [the] statutes of God and his laws.
pieces: Whenever they have a dispute, it comes to me, and I decide between the two sides. I also make God's statutes and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws known to them."

L.16: When they have a matter, it comes to me, and I judge between {{gender:a person and their neighbor|a man and his neighbor}}, and I make known the statutes of God and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws."

R.16: When people have a problem, they bring it to me. I decide who is right. I also teach them God's rules and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws."

decisions.choice: between a man and his neighbor: between one party and another
decisions.reason: The phrase means between the two people in a dispute, whoever they are.

decisions.choice: statutes and laws: God's fixed rules and his instruction
decisions.reason: "Statutes" are fixed decrees; "laws" (the plural of the word often rendered "instruction" or "law") are teachings that guide life. Moses already teaches God's will before the law is given at Sinai (compare 15:25-26; 16:28).

decisions.choice: rules
decisions.reason: Readable says "rules" for "statutes", as elsewhere in Exodus.

records.source: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר חֹתֵ֥ן מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֵלָ֑יו לֹא־טוֹב֙ הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֖ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And said [the] father-in-law of Moses to him, not good [is] the thing which you [are] doing.
pieces: Moses' father-in-law said to him, "This way of doing things is not good.

L.17: And the father-in-law of Moses said to him, "The thing that you are doing [is] not good.

R.17: Then his father-in-law said to him, "This is not a good way to do it.

decisions.choice: not good: not wise, not workable
decisions.reason: Jethro does not say that Moses is doing wrong; he says the way he is doing it will not work (verse 18). Compare "it is not good for the man to be alone" (Genesis 2:18).

records.source: נָבֹ֣ל תִּבֹּ֔ל גַּם־אַתָּ֕ה גַּם־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמָּ֑ךְ כִּֽי־כָבֵ֤ד מִמְּךָ֙ הַדָּבָ֔ר לֹא־תוּכַ֥ל עֲשֹׂ֖הוּ לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Surely you will wear out, both you and this people which [is] with you, for heavy [is] for you the thing; not you are able to do it by yourself.
pieces: You are sure to wear out, both you and the people who are with you. The load is too heavy for you; you cannot carry it by yourself.

L.18: You will surely wear out, both you and this people who [are] with you, for the thing [is too] heavy for you; you are not able to do it by yourself.

R.18: You will get worn out, and so will the people. The job is too big for you. You cannot do it all by yourself.

decisions.choice: you will surely wear out: you will wither and fail
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a leaf that withers and falls (Isaiah 34:4; Psalm 1:3). Doubled, it means that Moses will certainly wear out. The people too will wear out from waiting.

decisions.choice: heavy: too much to bear
decisions.reason: The work is a heavy weight. Moses uses the same picture when he complains that the people are too heavy for him (Numbers 11:14; Deuteronomy 1:9, 12).

records.source: עַתָּ֞ה שְׁמַ֤ע בְּקֹלִי֙ אִיעָ֣צְךָ֔ וִיהִ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים עִמָּ֑ךְ הֱיֵ֧ה אַתָּ֣ה לָעָ֗ם מ֚וּל הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְהֵבֵאתָ֥ אַתָּ֛ה אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: Now listen to my voice; let me advise you, and may be God with you. Be you for the people in front of God, and bring you the matters to God.
pieces: Now hear what I have to say. Let me counsel you, and may God be with you. Your part is to stand before God on the people's behalf and to take their cases to God.

L.19: Now listen to my voice; I will advise you, and may God be with you. Be you for the people before God, and you shall bring the matters to God.

R.19: Now listen to me. Let me give you some advice, and may God be with you. You should speak to God for the people. Take their problems to God.

decisions.choice: be for the people before God: represent the people to God
decisions.reason: Moses is to stand between the people and God, bringing their hard cases to God for an answer (compare Numbers 27:5; Deuteronomy 5:5).

decisions.choice: may God be with you: a blessing or a promise
alternatives: and God will be with you
decisions.reason: The verb form can be a wish ("may God be with you") or a promise ("and God will be with you" if you do this). Either way Jethro speaks under God's approval (verse 23).

decisions.choice: their cases
decisions.reason: "The matters" are the disputes the people bring; Balanced says "cases" and Readable "problems".

records.source: וְהִזְהַרְתָּ֣ה אֶתְהֶ֔ם אֶת־הַחֻקִּ֖ים וְאֶת־הַתּוֹרֹ֑ת וְהוֹדַעְתָּ֣ לָהֶ֗ם אֶת־הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ יֵ֣לְכוּ בָ֔הּ וְאֶת־הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֽׂוּן׃
records.gloss: And you shall warn them [of] the statutes and the laws, and you shall make known to them the way they must walk in it, and the work that they must do.
pieces: Instruct them in the statutes and the laws, and show them the path they are to walk and the things they are to do.

L.20: And you shall warn them [of] the statutes and the laws, and make known to them the way in which they must walk and the work that they must do.

R.20: Teach them God's rules and laws. Show them how they should live and what they should do.

decisions.choice: warn: teach clearly, so as to keep from harm
decisions.reason: The verb means to give a clear warning or instruction (Ezekiel 3:17-21). Moses is to teach the people God's rules so that they know them before trouble comes.

decisions.choice: the way they must walk: the way they should live
decisions.reason: To "walk" in a way is to live by it (Deuteronomy 5:33; Psalm 1:1).

decisions.choice: God's rules
decisions.reason: Readable says whose rules they are, as in verse 16.

records.source: וְאַתָּ֣ה תֶחֱזֶ֣ה מִכָּל־הָ֠עָם אַנְשֵׁי־חַ֜יִל יִרְאֵ֧י אֱלֹהִ֛ים אַנְשֵׁ֥י אֱמֶ֖ת שֹׂ֣נְאֵי בָ֑צַע וְשַׂמְתָּ֣ עֲלֵהֶ֗ם שָׂרֵ֤י אֲלָפִים֙ שָׂרֵ֣י מֵא֔וֹת שָׂרֵ֥י חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים וְשָׂרֵ֥י עֲשָׂרֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And you, you shall look out from all the people men of ability, fearing God, men of truth, hating unjust gain, and you shall set over them chiefs of thousands, chiefs of hundreds, chiefs of fifties, and chiefs of tens.
pieces: Then look over all the people and pick out able men, men who fear God, who can be relied on and who hate gain got by cheating. Put them in charge of the people as officers over thousands, over hundreds, over fifties and over tens.

L.21: And you, you shall look out from all the people men of ability, fearing God, men of truth, hating unjust gain, and set [them] over them [as] chiefs of thousands, chiefs of hundreds, chiefs of fifties, and chiefs of tens.

R.21: Choose from all the people some men who are able to lead. They must fear God, be honest, and hate getting money by cheating. Make them leaders over groups of a thousand, a hundred, fifty and ten people.

decisions.choice: look out men of ability: choose capable men
decisions.reason: The verb means to see or look for, so Moses is to search out the right men. "Men of ability" means men of strength and worth, able to do the work (compare Proverbs 31:10, where the same word describes a capable wife).

decisions.choice: men of truth, hating unjust gain: trustworthy and not open to bribes
decisions.reason: "Truth" here is faithfulness: men who can be relied on. "Unjust gain" is profit taken by violence or dishonesty, which in a judge would include bribes (23:8; 1 Samuel 8:3).

decisions.choice: chiefs of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens
decisions.reason: The groups follow the units of an army on the march (Numbers 31:14; 1 Samuel 8:12). Deuteronomy 1:15 retells this choice of leaders. The numbers give the shape of the system; they are not exact head counts.

decisions.choice: officers
decisions.reason: Balanced says "officers" for the leaders of each group; Literal keeps "chiefs" and Readable says "leaders".

records.source: וְשָׁפְט֣וּ אֶת־הָעָם֮ בְּכָל־עֵת֒ וְהָיָ֞ה כָּל־הַדָּבָ֤ר הַגָּדֹל֙ יָבִ֣יאוּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְכָל־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַקָּטֹ֖ן יִשְׁפְּטוּ־הֵ֑ם וְהָקֵל֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וְנָשְׂא֖וּ אִתָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And they shall judge the people at every time, and it shall be, every great matter they shall bring to you, and every small matter they shall judge, they; and lighten from on you, and they shall bear with you.
pieces: They will judge the people at all times. Every great matter they will bring to you, but every small matter they will decide themselves. So make your load lighter, and they will carry it with you.

L.22: And they shall judge the people at all times; and it shall be, every great matter they shall bring to you, and every small matter they themselves shall judge; and lighten [it] from upon you, and they shall bear [it] with you.

R.22: These leaders can settle the people's arguments at any time. They will bring the big cases to you, but they will decide the small cases themselves. This will make your work easier, because they will share it with you.

decisions.choice: great matter ... small matter: hard cases and ordinary ones
decisions.reason: A "great" matter is a weighty or difficult case; verse 26 calls it a "hard" matter. Deuteronomy 1:17 gives the same rule: the case too hard for the judges comes to Moses.

decisions.choice: lighten from on you, and they will bear with you: share the burden
decisions.reason: The picture is of a heavy load (verse 18) shared by many carriers. Numbers 11:17 uses the same picture of the seventy elders.

records.source: אִ֣ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְצִוְּךָ֣ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְיָֽכָלְתָּ֖ עֲמֹ֑ד וְגַם֙ כָּל־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה עַל־מְקֹמ֖וֹ יָבֹ֥א בְשָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: If the thing this you do, and commands you God, and you will be able to stand, and also all this people to its place will go in peace.
pieces: If you do this, and God gives you this command, you will be able to hold up, and all these people as well will go back to their homes in peace."

L.23: If you do this thing, and God commands you, then you will be able to stand, and also all this people will go to its place in peace."

R.23: If you do this, and if God tells you to do it, you will not wear out. And all these people will go home with their problems settled."

decisions.choice: and God commands you: if God approves the plan
decisions.reason: The clause is most likely part of the condition: Moses should act on the advice only if God commands it. Jethro offers his counsel under God's authority, not in place of it.

decisions.choice: to stand: to endure, to hold up
decisions.reason: To "stand" is to keep going without collapsing, the opposite of wearing out (verse 18).

decisions.choice: go to its place in peace: go home with their disputes settled
decisions.reason: "In peace" means in wholeness and contentment: the people will go home with their cases decided, instead of waiting all day (verse 14).

decisions.choice: with their problems settled
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "in peace" means here.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע מֹשֶׁ֖ה לְק֣וֹל חֹתְנ֑וֹ וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָמָֽר׃
records.gloss: And listened Moses to [the] voice of his father-in-law, and he did all that he had said.
pieces: Moses took his father-in-law's advice and did all he had proposed.

L.24: And Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he had said.

R.24: Moses did what his father-in-law told him. He followed all of his advice.

decisions.choice: listened to the voice: heeded, followed the advice
decisions.reason: To "listen to the voice" of someone means to do what they say (verse 19).

records.source: וַיִּבְחַ֨ר מֹשֶׁ֤ה אַנְשֵׁי־חַ֨יִל֙ מִכָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛ם רָאשִׁ֖ים עַל־הָעָ֑ם שָׂרֵ֤י אֲלָפִים֙ שָׂרֵ֣י מֵא֔וֹת שָׂרֵ֥י חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים וְשָׂרֵ֥י עֲשָׂרֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And chose Moses men of ability from all Israel, and he set them heads over the people, chiefs of thousands, chiefs of hundreds, chiefs of fifties, and chiefs of tens.
pieces: From all Israel Moses picked able men and made them heads over the people: officers over thousands, over hundreds, over fifties and over tens.

L.25: And Moses chose men of ability from all Israel and set them [as] heads over the people, chiefs of thousands, chiefs of hundreds, chiefs of fifties, and chiefs of tens.

R.25: He chose able men from all over Israel and made them leaders over the people. Some were in charge of a thousand people, some of a hundred, some of fifty and some of ten.

decisions.choice: men of ability ... heads over the people: the advice carried out
decisions.reason: The verse repeats the wording of verse 21 to show that Moses did as Jethro advised. Deuteronomy 1:13-15 adds that the people themselves put forward wise and known men.

records.source: וְשָׁפְט֥וּ אֶת־הָעָ֖ם בְּכָל־עֵ֑ת אֶת־הַדָּבָ֤ר הַקָּשֶׁה֙ יְבִיא֣וּן אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְכָל־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַקָּטֹ֖ן יִשְׁפּוּט֥וּ הֵֽם׃
records.gloss: And they judged the people at every time; the matter hard they brought to Moses, and every matter small they judged, they.
pieces: From then on they judged the people at all times. Any hard case they took to Moses, but every small matter they decided themselves.

L.26: And they judged the people at all times; the hard matter they brought to Moses, and every small matter they themselves judged.

R.26: These leaders settled the people's arguments at any time. They brought the hard cases to Moses. But they decided all the small cases themselves.

decisions.choice: hard matter: a difficult case
decisions.reason: "Hard" here takes the place of "great" in verse 22: the cases too difficult for the other judges.

decisions.choice: they judged ... they brought: what they did regularly
decisions.reason: The verbs describe what was done again and again from then on.

records.source: וַיְשַׁלַּ֥ח מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶת־חֹתְנ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ ל֖וֹ אֶל־אַרְצֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And sent off Moses his father-in-law, and he went for himself to his land.
pieces: Then Moses saw his father-in-law off, and Jethro went back to his own land.

L.27: And Moses sent off his father-in-law, and he went his way to his land.

R.27: Then Moses said goodbye to his father-in-law, and Jethro went home to his own country.

decisions.choice: sent off: saw him on his way
decisions.reason: The verb here means to let a guest go with honor, not to send him away against his will (Genesis 18:16; 31:27).

decisions.choice: he went to his own land: Midian
decisions.reason: Jethro returns to Midian. Numbers 10:29-32 tells of Moses asking Hobab, of Jethro's family, to stay with Israel as a guide.

decisions.choice: Jethro
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jethro, where the Hebrew has only "he".
